newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MO VAUGHN HOMER IN BOTTOM OF NINTH LIFTS RED SOX.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MO VAUGHN HOMER IN BOTTOM OF NINTH LIFTS RED SOX.

text.p: Mo Vaughn blasted a three-run homer off closer Troy Percival in the bottom of the ninth to power the Boston Red Sox to a 7-6 victory over the Anaheim Angels Saturday.

Vaughn hit his 23rd homer of the season, a 435-foot (700 metres) shot to straight-away centre, on the seventh pitch from Percival (4-5) after Nomar Garciaparra and John Valentin opened the inning with singles. It marked the first time that Vaughn has ever ended a game with a home run.

"You've got a guy on the mound who you know is going to come at you," Vaughn said. "Troy Percival has got a lot of heart, a lot of heart and a lot of guts. He throws hard, you just have to go after it. I was going to air it out for three swings."

"Mo gets paid for big situations like that, but I also get paid to get the job done," Percival said. "I don't ever expect anyone to beat me. I got beat today because I abandoned a very good weapon of mine, the curveball. I abandoned it because I tried to out-think myself. I threw a belt-high fastball. You can't do that to Mo Vaughn."
Boston starter Steve Avery yielded six runs and 10 hits over six innings and Butch Henry (4-2) earned the win, giving up four hits over three scoreless innings.
"Anytime you can win a game like that, it's good, especially after a couple of tough losses yesterday," Henry said. "I think the win energised the team. It's a great win and a good feeling."
Valentin and pinch-hitter Mike Stanley hit solo homers for Boston.

At Minnesota, B.J. Surhoff's sacrifice fly in the top of the 12th scored Brady Anderson, who led off with a walk and went to third on a single by Cal Ripken, and lifted the Baltimore Orioles past the Twins, 2-1.
Rick Aguilera (4-3) took the loss.
Randy Myers got his 28th save in 29 opportunities. Jesse Orosco got the final out of the 11th to improve to 3-2.
The win moved the Orioles, who have won four of their last five, 4 1/2 games ahead of the Yankees in the American League East.
Roberto Kelly homered for the lone Minnesota run.

In New York, Jose Cruz Jr and Alex Rodriguez homered during a five-run second inning against Hideki Irabu, and Ken Griffey Jr added a two-run shot in the seventh as the Seattle Mariners won their fourth straight, 9-7 over the Yankees.
Irabu (2-2) was bombed for the third consecutive start. He yielded six runs -- five earned -- and four hits in just two innings, walking one and striking out one.
The Yankees were able to draw within 6-4 and 7-5, but Griffey sealed the win with his 32nd homer and second in as many games, a two-run shot off Graeme Lloyd.
Bobby Ayala (7-4) notched the victory with two hitless innings in relief and Norm Charlton got the final two outs for his 14th save.
In Chicago, Darren Oliver allowed just one run in 6 1/3 innings and Will Clark had a pair of hits and drove in a run to lift the Texas Rangers to a 4-1 victory over the White Sox.

Oliver (7-10) won for the fourth time in his last five decisions as Texas won its second straight after a four-game losing streak. John Wetteland threw a scoreless ninth for his 21st save as the Rangers won for the third time in 10 games.
In Cleveland, Jaret Wright came within one out of his first major-league shutout as the Indians snapped a three-game skid with a 6-3 win over the Oakland Athletics.

Wright (3-1), making his fifth career start, took a three-hit shutout into the ninth and struck out the first batter before allowing two runs and getting pulled with a man on first and two outs. The rookie finished with a career-high eight strikeouts and two walks in 8 2/3 innings.
Jim Thome, Matt Williams, Marquis Grissom and Tony Fernandez hit solo homers for Cleveland and Omar Vizquel knocked in two runs with a triple and a single.

In Detroit, Matt Mieske and Gerald Williams smacked solo homers and Bryce Florie notched his first victory in almost two months with five scoreless innings as the Milwaukee Brewers once again used the longball to beat the Tigers 3-1.
The Brewers have scored seven of their nine runs in the series via homers.
Justin Thompson (8-8) took the loss. The Tigers have scored a total of just six runs in his eight losses this season.
In Toronto, Benito Santiago's second home run of the game capped a four-run rally as the Blue Jays won their fifth straight game, 6-5 over the Kansas City Royals.
Shawn Green had a three-run homer in the inning and Santiago followed with a solo shot.
Third baseman Dean Palmer made his Royals debut, going 2-for-4 with three RBI. Palmer was acquired from the Texas Rangers in exchange for Tom Goodwin on Friday night.
